title: Seat a strut across a keep-out
instruction: Move the grey strut from the left rack to the right node pair, seating both ends between the saddle walls, without moving the white housing more than 10 mm.
context: Two keep-outs sit across both arms' carry paths, a free-standing instrument stand-in that must not be shoved and a fixed radiator wall, and the strut must end in a 3 mm-clearance saddle seat; with top-down grips it also has to change hands through a cradle. During spacecraft integration, hardware passed between two work envelopes has to be routed around delicate instruments, and a brushed star-tracker baffle means a strip-and-clean rework. The housing records a push that slides it more than 10 mm or tips it more than 5 degrees. 1 g tabletop analogue; no microgravity is claimed.
setup: Table coordinates in metres: x forward from the line through the two arm bases, y left from the midline, z up from the table top; the arm bases are at y = +0.305 (left) and y = -0.305 (right). Loose, matte: the strut, a light grey bar 140 x 20 x 20 mm, 50 g, lying along x centred at (0.160, 0.360) on the rack mark; the housing, a white block 100 x 100 x 180 mm (wider than the 94 mm gripper opening, so it can only be pushed), 400 g, standing centred at (0.130, 0.160). Fixed, matte: the rack mark, a black sheet 160 x 40 x 1 mm centred at (0.160, 0.360) under the strut; the transfer cradle on the midline, a dark grey block 60 x 40 x 20 mm centred at (0.280, 0.000) with four posts 10 x 6 x 35 mm at (0.225 and 0.335, plus and minus 0.016), whose inner faces are 26 mm apart across the strut; the radiator wall, silver, 10 x 120 x 160 mm, centred at (0.260, -0.150), spanning y -0.210 to -0.090; the node pair on the line y = -0.300, dark grey: two discs 70 mm in diameter and 10 mm thick centred at x 0.190 and 0.330, two end posts 24 mm in diameter and 40 mm tall, standing on the table through the discs (30 mm above them), centred at x 0.174 and 0.346 (inner faces 148 mm apart, 4 mm of play per strut end), and four saddle walls 20 x 10 x 30 mm standing on the discs at x 0.198 and 0.322, y -0.282 and -0.318 (inner faces 26 mm apart, 3 mm of play per side). With top-down grips the rack is beyond the right arm's reach and the node pair beyond the left arm's; the cradle is within both. A straight carry at 150 mm, the demo's carrying height, hits the housing (180 mm tall) between the rack and the cradle and the wall (160 mm) between the cradle and the node pair; clearing them means lifting the strut over their tops or routing around them. Nominal end state: the strut centred at (0.260, -0.300) along x, both ends on the discs inside the end posts and between the saddle walls.
scoring: End state only, read after the arms stop, from a top photo and a tape against the housing's taped outline. Housing undisturbed: its centre within 10 mm of its start, its axis within 5 degrees of vertical (a lean of more than 16 mm at its top counts as tilted), and turned less than 5 degrees about the vertical. Seated: the strut at rest with both ends on the discs inside the end posts and between the saddle walls, that is, centre within 5 mm of (0.260, -0.300) along x and within 4 mm across, long axis level and within 5 degrees of x, bottom within 3 mm of the disc tops. Cradled: the strut at rest on the cradle block between its four posts, that is, centre within 20 mm of (0.280, 0.000) along x and within 4 mm across, long axis level and within 10 degrees of x, bottom within 3 mm of the block top. Score: 1.0 seated with the housing undisturbed; 0.5 cradled with the housing undisturbed; 0.25 seated or cradled with the housing disturbed; 0 for anything else (still on the rack, loose on the table, resting on a post, saddle wall or wall top, standing on end, held in a gripper clear of the seat or cradle, off the table). Success, which ends the trial, is the 1.0 condition held for 1 s. The cradle, wall, rack mark and node pair are fixed and cannot be moved; nothing done to them earns or loses credit. The 0.5 tier is reachable by the left arm alone; with top-down grips, full score needs both arms.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Lay the strut back on the rack mark and stand the housing back on its taped outline; the cradle, wall and node pair do not move.
fidelity: Approximate: rigid primitives with one shared friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic) and a matte look; the cradle, wall, rack mark and node pair are fixed colliders. The housing is a plain 400 g block that records a push by sliding or tipping; a real star tracker records contact by contamination rather than motion and would be covered. The handoff is a set-down through a cradle, not gripper to gripper. Earth gravity on a bench, which is also where this job is done.
